inputs.original_text: President Luis Abinader is over in France pushing the Dominican Republic into global transparency standards, but this is clearly just another elite move to look reform-minded while dodging the real roots of the problem. On 25 March 2026, Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Paris to create the country's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, witnessed by President Abinader. These deals get sold as progress, yet they sidestep the structural inequalities and historical power imbalances that fuel corruption and leave workers and marginalized communities exposed. Real change requires institutional reform centered on labor rights and protections for the vulnerable, not partnerships with bodies like the OECD that shield existing systems of inequality.

On 25 March 2026, Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Paris to create the country's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, witnessed by President Abinader. These deals get pitched as progress, yet they sidestep the structural inequalities and historical power imbalances that drive corruption and leave workers and marginalized communities exposed. Real change requires institutional reform centered on labor rights and protections for the vulnerable, not partnerships with bodies like the OECD that shield existing systems of inequality.
